name: Gcore
snippet: Luxembourg edge cloud and CDN provider that also rents NVIDIA GPUs up to GB300 NVL72. It reported about $140M in 2025 revenue and launched GPU VMs in a sovereign AI region in Portugal in March 2026.
origin: Andre Reitenbach founded Gcore in Luxembourg in 2014. The company built its own content delivery network for the gaming industry and later added hosting, security and public cloud services. It began building GPU cloud capacity in 2021 and opened a generative AI cluster in Luxembourg with LuxConnect in October 2023. Gcore took no outside money until July 2024, when Wargaming led a $60M Series A meant for NVIDIA GPU servers.
today: Gcore reports about $140M in 2025 revenue, up from just under $76M at the end of 2023, and CEO Andre Reitenbach puts the 2025 figure at about €120M. It runs more than 210 points of presence with over 200 Tbps of network capacity and employs about 550 people. Its GPU cloud offers NVIDIA A100, H100, H200, B300 and GB300 NVL72 systems with InfiniBand, on demand or reserved. In March 2026 it launched GPU virtual machines on NVIDIA Hopper, starting in Sines-3, its sovereign AI region in Portugal. Named AI customers include Aleph Alpha, Higgsfield and Leonardo AI.
platform: Gcore sells bare metal and virtual GPU servers alongside its CDN, DDoS protection and edge network. Everywhere Inference runs trained models on edge nodes across more than 180 points of presence, with cloud, on-premise and hybrid deployment options. The Everywhere AI platform, launched in November 2025, added managed Slurm, integrated JupyterLab and token-based inference billing in March 2026. Gcore also licenses AI Cloud Stack, software that turns raw NVIDIA clusters into multi-tenant clouds for telcos and service providers, and says it has run on thousands of Hopper GPUs in Europe.
outlook: Gcore positions itself as a European sovereign alternative to the US hyperscalers for AI training and inference. Its GPU cloud page lists GB200 as upcoming and GB300 NVL72 racks on request, and the company does not publish the size of its own GPU fleet. The company says it plans more points of presence and more hires. The last outside funding it has announced is the 2024 Series A.

name: Verda
snippet: Helsinki GPU cloud, formerly DataCrunch, running NVIDIA GPUs up to GB300 NVL72 in Finland and Iceland. It raised a $189M Series B in September 2026 at a valuation above $1B.
origin: Ruben Bryon founded the company in Helsinki in 2020 as DataCrunch to give developers on-demand GPU capacity without the barriers of traditional clouds. It grew as a self-service NVIDIA GPU cloud in its own Nordic data centers, which run on renewable energy. The company rebranded as Verda in late 2025 and says it wants to build a European hyperscaler focused on data protection and renewable power.
today: Verda raised a €164.8M ($189M) Series B led by Emergence Capital in September 2026, which made it a unicorn and took total funding above $450M. Supermicro, MUFG Innovation Partners, Varma and Tesi joined the round. The company reports a $165M annualized revenue run rate as of July 2026 and says it is cash-flow positive. In April 2026 it closed a €100M package of equity and debt from Nordic lenders, after a €55M Series A in September 2025. It runs data centers in Finland and Iceland and has about 250 staff, with new offices in London and San Francisco.
platform: Verda sells GPU instances, self-service instant clusters with InfiniBand, serverless GPU containers for inference and batch jobs, and block, shared file and container registry storage. Its fleet runs from A100 to GB300 NVL72, and Supermicro supplies its liquid-cooled GB300 NVL72, HGX B300, HGX B200 and RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell systems. The company offers confidential computing for hardware-attested inference and fine-tuning. An in-house AI lab works with customers such as 1X and gives compute to the SGLang and vLLM open-source projects.
outlook: Verda plans to use the Series B to build inference products, add compute capacity over the next year and expand across Europe, the US and Asia. In April 2026 it said it would hire more than 100 people by the end of the year. The company competes on price and says its services cost up to 90% less than AWS, Azure and Google Cloud.

name: Hyperstack
snippet: GPU cloud platform of London-based NexGen Cloud, offering NVIDIA GPUs up to GB300 NVL72 in Europe and North America. It took a $34M GPU-backed loan in June 2026 to fund B200s in Sweden.
origin: Chris Starkey and Youlian Tzanev founded NexGen Cloud in London in October 2020. In October 2023 the company announced a $1B plan for an AI Supercloud of more than 20,000 NVIDIA H100 GPUs in European data centers, with $576M of hardware already on order. It launched Hyperstack in 2023 as an on-demand GPU service for AI startups and enterprises.
today: NexGen Cloud raised a $45M Series A in April 2025 at a $354M valuation from high-net-worth individuals and family trusts, and reported £72M in revenue for 2023 to 2024. Hyperstack has more than 10,000 users. DCD reports that the company runs many thousands of GPUs but has not deployed the full 20,000 it planned. In June 2026 USD.AI provided a $34M three-year non-recourse facility, secured by the GPUs and their contracts, to fund a B200 fleet in Sweden. The company says it will add 4,500 B300 GPUs in its EU2 Finland data center later in 2026 and 56 MW of capacity in 2027. It moved into a new City of London headquarters in May 2026 and named a new CFO and CRO.
platform: Hyperstack offers on-demand and spot GPU virtual machines, reserved clusters through Hyperstack Secure Private Cloud, on-demand Kubernetes and object storage, with billing by the minute. Its AI Studio adds tools to fine-tune, deploy and monitor models and connects to Hugging Face. The company says its data centers in Europe and North America run on 100% renewable energy. It holds NVIDIA Cloud Partner status and gained SOC 2 Type 2 attestation in July 2026.
outlook: NexGen Cloud pitches itself as a sovereign-by-design provider for regulated UK and European customers. It plans to bring HGX B300 to on-demand and reserved clusters and to grow capacity in Finland and Sweden with asset-backed debt. The company plans hiring across engineering, infrastructure, sales and operations through 2026.

name: Scaleway
snippet: Paris cloud provider owned by Iliad that rents GPU instances up to NVIDIA B300 and runs H100 clusters used by Mistral AI. The European Commission picked it in April 2026 for a €180M sovereign cloud framework.

facts.label: OpCore capacity under construction near Paris

origin: Xavier Niel founded the company in 1999 as Online SAS, a French hosting provider that became part of his Iliad telecom group. It grew into one of France's largest hosts, with data centers around Paris that include DC4 in a former fallout shelter and DC5 in a converted postal sorting center. Under the Scaleway name it moved into public cloud. In 2023 it built Nabu, a 1,016 GPU NVIDIA H100 cluster that Mistral AI used to develop Mixtral.
today: Scaleway rents B300-SXM, H100-SXM, H100 PCIe, L40S and L4 GPU instances billed by the minute in its Paris and Warsaw regions, and builds custom H100 clusters on InfiniBand for model labs. Customers include Mistral AI, Kyutai, which trained its Moshi voice model there, and H Company. Iliad has announced a €3B investment program in cloud and AI. In 2026 Scaleway opened a Milan region, won a place on a €180M European Commission sovereign cloud framework, signed a trusted cloud contract with Airbus and bought the HPC firm Qarnot. OpCore, the data center business linked to Iliad, says it has 730 MW under construction around Paris backed by €4B of investment.
platform: Scaleway's GPU instances connect to its Kapsule managed Kubernetes, object storage and Managed Inference service, and its Generative APIs serve open models such as GLM-5.2. Its custom clusters use NVIDIA ConnectX-7 and Quantum-2 InfiniBand at 400 Gb/s, DDN storage and Slurm for job scheduling. The DC5 data center that hosts the H100 clusters runs on renewable energy with a PUE of 1.16.
outlook: Scaleway plans new regions in Sweden and Germany and markets itself as fully European-owned, with all teams and data in Europe. The Qarnot deal adds liquid-cooled HPC that recovers server heat for district heating. Its public GPU list tops out at B300 instances, and it has not published the size of any Blackwell cluster.

name: Sesterce
snippet: French AI infrastructure company that rents NVIDIA GPUs and is developing large AI campuses. It plans a 1 GW site in Bosquel with SoftBank and a €10B campus in Jämsä, Finland.
origin: Sesterce is a French AI infrastructure company led by co-founder and CEO Youssef El Manssouri. It sells on-demand GPU virtual machines and bare metal servers and now puts most of its effort into building its own AI supercomputer campuses. The company says it operates in France, the United States and Singapore.
today: In June 2026 Sesterce and SoftBank Group announced a joint venture to develop a 1 GW AI data center in Bosquel in the Somme, with a €10M fund for the Hauts-de-France region. In October 2026 it set a 40 MW cap for its Rovaltain campus near Valence, where it holds a building permit but has paused work to add community commitments. Two days later it announced plans to invest more than €10B in a campus at the former Kaipola paper mill in Jämsä, Finland, starting with 200 MW, then 600 MW, and aiming for more than 1 GW in Finland. Its cloud lists NVIDIA H100, H200, B200, A100, L40S and RTX 5090 instances across North America, Europe and Asia.
platform: Sesterce offers on-demand VMs and bare metal servers with no commitment, plus dedicated single-tenant bare-metal clusters with root access and out-of-band management. Its campuses use Sesterce Modular Design, a set of factory-built power and cooling modules, and Sesterce OS, software that monitors each campus from the grid to the GPU. The campuses use closed-loop direct liquid cooling topped up with rainwater and recycled water.
outlook: Every Sesterce campus follows six commitments, including one megawatt of new renewable generation on the same grid for each megawatt consumed within ten years and a €10M community fund. The company has not disclosed total financing or GPU orders for its campuses. It is hiring for construction, grid, liquid cooling and GPU fleet roles in Paris, San Francisco, Seattle and Helsinki.

name: OVHcloud
snippet: French cloud provider listed on Euronext Paris with 46 data centers and €1.08B in fiscal 2025 revenue. It rents NVIDIA H200, H100 and L40S GPUs and serves open models through AI Endpoints.
origin: Octave Klaba founded OVH in 1999 while a student in Lille to meet demand for internet hosting. The company built water-cooled data centers and its own fiber network and expanded across Europe from 2004. It entered cloud with Hosted Private Cloud, rebranded as OVHcloud in 2019 and listed on Euronext Paris in October 2021.
today: OVHcloud passed €1B in revenue in fiscal 2025, reaching €1,084.6M with 9.3% like-for-like growth and a 40.4% adjusted EBITDA margin. Octave Klaba returned as chairman and CEO in October 2025. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026 revenue rose 6.9% organically to €289.6M, with Public Cloud up 20.2%. The company runs 46 data centers for 1.6 million customers. It front-loaded capex in the first half of fiscal 2026 to secure hardware as component costs rose. The European Commission selected it for a €180M sovereign cloud contract, and it bought Gladia, a speech-to-text company, and Dragon LLM to build AI services.
platform: OVHcloud's public cloud rents NVIDIA H200, H100, L40S, L4, A10 and V100S GPUs in instances of 1 to 4 GPUs. AI Endpoints, launched in April 2025, is a serverless, pay-per-token API for more than 40 open-weight models hosted from its Gravelines data center. In June 2026 its OVH Labs unit previewed OVHai Workspace, an open collaborative agentic AI platform.
outlook: OVHcloud guides to 5% to 7% organic revenue growth for fiscal 2026 with capex at 33% to 35% of revenue. A new five-year plan started on September 1, 2026, after a refinancing that runs through 2030. The company is reorganizing sales around digital natives and corporate clients and building a defence vertical. Its CFO stepped down in August 2026.

name: Hetzner
snippet: German hosting company known for low-cost dedicated servers. It rents single-GPU dedicated servers with NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell cards from €214 a month.
origin: Martin Hetzner founded the company in 1997 in Gunzenhausen, Bavaria. It became one of Europe's largest hosting providers by selling dedicated servers at low prices from its own data center parks. It runs sites in Nuremberg and Falkenstein in Germany and Helsinki in Finland, plus Ashburn, Hillsboro and Singapore.
today: Hetzner rents dedicated servers with one NVIDIA professional GPU each and does not list multi-GPU training clusters. The GEX131, launched in December 2025, pairs an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q with 96 GB of memory for €889 a month or about €1.42 an hour. It added the GEX45 with an RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell SFF for €214 a month in September 2026 and the GEX63 with an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q for €999 a month in October 2026. The GPU servers run in its German and Finnish data centers. Hetzner announced a price adjustment effective April 2026 and changed setup fees twice in 2026.
platform: Hetzner's GPU servers are dedicated bare-metal machines ordered through its server configurator, with monthly or hourly billing and one-time setup fees. The GEX131 uses an Intel Xeon Gold 5412U with 256 GB of DDR5 ECC memory, and the GEX63 uses an Intel Core Ultra 7 265 with 128 GB. The company markets the GEX45 for inference and the larger models for training.
outlook: Hetzner adds GPU models one card generation at a time and broke ground on a new headquarters in Gunzenhausen in October 2026. It has not announced multi-GPU nodes or data center scale AI clusters.

name: Tatra Supercompute
snippet: Slovak startup planning an AI data center and supercomputer built on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. It has published few details beyond its founding team and a stated NVIDIA supplier agreement.
origin: Tatra Supercompute presents itself as a project to build an AI data center in Slovakia that pairs AI computing with green energy. Its founders include CEO and COO Peter Novak, a banking and telecom executive who has led data center projects, and president Robert Lesko, who spent 25 years at Morgan Stanley.
today: The company's website says it has a supplier agreement with NVIDIA for Blackwell GPUs and that the facility will rank among the most powerful supercomputers in the world. It names no site, power capacity, funding, customers or launch date.
outlook: The company says the data center will draw on electricity generated in Slovakia and help build a Slovak AI business ecosystem. The website gives no timeline for financing or construction.

name: Firebird
snippet: AI cloud building NVIDIA AI factories in Armenia, starting with 6,144 B200 GPUs in Hrazdan that opened in August 2026. Perplexity is an early customer, and a $4B second phase targets 50,000 GPUs.
origin: Razmig Hovaghimian and Alexander Yesayan co-founded Firebird in 2025 to build US-stack AI compute in emerging markets with clean power. In June 2025 it announced a $500M public-private partnership with the Government of Armenia, NVIDIA and Team Group to build an AI cloud of thousands of Blackwell GPUs. Noubar Afeyan of Flagship Pioneering is a founding partner, investor and advisor. Bloomberg reported in November 2025 that the US approved its use of NVIDIA chips in Armenia.
today: Firebird opened its first AI factory, DC-1 in Hrazdan, Armenia, in August 2026 with 6,144 liquid-cooled NVIDIA B200 GPUs. Armenia's prime minister, Jensen Huang and Michael Dell attended the opening, where Firebird named Perplexity as one of its first customers. In February 2026 US Vice President JD Vance announced a $4B second phase targeting 50,000 GPUs in 2026, including 41,000 GB300s. CoreWeave invested earlier in 2026, and NVIDIA says it intends to invest. In June 2026 Firebird signed agreements with the Government of Kazakhstan, where it says it has secured 125 MW at Data Center Valley.
platform: Firebird Cloud provisions B200 instances through a console or API and lets customers run Kubernetes or Slurm on liquid-cooled Blackwell clusters with InfiniBand networking. Managed inference endpoints for open-source models are listed as coming soon. The company says DC-1 reached NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud status for training on B200, performing at 99% or more of NVIDIA's reference results.
outlook: Firebird plans to expand to 300 MW in Armenia and to more than 70,000 NVIDIA Rubin and Blackwell GPUs by the end of 2027. It targets 2 GW of capacity across Armenia, Kazakhstan and other markets by the end of 2028. Its website lists DC-2 in Hrazdan with Vera Rubin GPUs and a planned DC-3 in Kazakhstan, and different pages give different power and GPU figures for both.

name: DigitalOcean
snippet: US developer cloud listed on the NYSE that rents NVIDIA and AMD GPUs and sells inference to AI-native companies. Its AI customer ARR reached $234M in Q2 2026, up 212% year over year.
origin: Ben and Moisey Uretsky, Jeff Carr, Alec Hartman and Mitch Wainer founded DigitalOcean in 2011 to sell simple virtual servers to developers. It grew into a cloud for developers and small businesses and went public on the NYSE in March 2021. It bought the GPU cloud Paperspace to add AI and machine learning products. In March 2025 it partnered with Flexential to add NVIDIA H200 and AMD Instinct capacity.
today: DigitalOcean reported $281M in second-quarter 2026 revenue, up 29%, and raised its 2026 guidance to $1.17B to $1.18B. AI customer ARR reached $234M, and the company says 85% of it comes from inference and core cloud rather than bare metal. Remaining performance obligations rose to $894M, including its first nine-figure annual customer commitments. It has about 155 MW of committed data center capacity, including 20 MW added for 2027 and 2028. A follow-on share offering in the first quarter of 2026 raised $888M net, and it used $500M of that to repay debt.
platform: GPU Droplets are single-GPU and 8-GPU virtual machines with NVIDIA HGX B300, H200 and H100, L40S and RTX Ada cards, or AMD Instinct MI350X, MI325X and MI300X, billed per second. GPU capacity sits in its New York, Toronto, Atlanta, Richmond and Amsterdam regions. Its AI-Native Cloud, launched in 2026, adds an Inference Engine that routes requests across more than 75 models, managed agents, bare metal GPUs and Kubernetes with GPU support.
outlook: CEO Paddy Srinivasan expects growth to reach 35% or more by the fourth quarter of 2026 and to exceed 50% in 2027. Third-quarter guidance is $304M to $307M. The company is moving from small monthly accounts toward large AI contracts, and its weighted average contract life has risen from 1.6 years to more than 3 years.

name: Vultr
snippet: Florida developer cloud with more than 30 regions that rents NVIDIA and AMD GPUs alongside general cloud. Backed by AMD, it is building a $1B, 50 MW AMD GPU cluster in Ohio.
origin: David Aninowsky founded Vultr in 2014 as a cloud for developers. It grew into a general-purpose cloud with compute, storage, networking and bare metal in more than 30 regions on six continents. It added GPU-as-a-service as AI demand grew and built close ties with AMD.
today: Vultr raised $333M at a $3.5B valuation in December 2024 in a round led by AMD and LuminArx Capital Management. In 2025 it added $329M in credit financing from lenders including Bank of America, Citi and Goldman Sachs. Bloomberg reported in December 2025 that it would spend more than $1B on a 50 MW cluster of AMD chips in Ohio, due to launch in the first quarter of 2026. Its bare metal catalog lists 8-GPU AMD MI355X, MI325X and MI300X servers and 8-GPU NVIDIA B200, H100 and A100 servers, plus GH200 and L40S machines. J.J. Kardwell is CEO.
platform: Vultr sells cloud GPU virtual machines, bare metal GPU servers, Kubernetes and a serverless inference service on the same platform as its CPU instances and object storage. Its public API prices an 8-GPU AMD MI355X server at $20.72 an hour and an 8-GPU NVIDIA B200 server at $68 an hour. Cloud GPU plans start at a single NVIDIA L40S billed by the hour.
outlook: Vultr ties much of its AI expansion to AMD, its investor and chip supplier, and funds GPU purchases partly with bank credit. The Ohio cluster is its largest announced build. The company does not disclose revenue or total GPU fleet size.

name: Latitude.sh
snippet: Bare metal cloud, formerly Maxihost, with 26 locations and NVIDIA GPU clusters, now owned by Megaport. Its parent raised about $594M in July 2026 to build a global AI inference cloud on it.
origin: Latitude.sh grew out of Maxihost, a bare metal hosting provider whose domain now points to Latitude.sh. It built a developer-first platform that provisions dedicated servers through an API in seconds, serving blockchain nodes, SaaS, gaming, adtech and streaming customers. It later added dedicated NVIDIA GPU clusters for inference, fine-tuning and training.
today: Megaport, the Brisbane-based network-as-a-service provider listed on the ASX, agreed in November 2025 to acquire Latitude.sh and expected to close by the end of that year. At the time Latitude had more than 7,700 servers and 1,150 customers in 20 markets across 10 countries, and it now lists 26 locations. In July 2026 Megaport announced a capital raise of A$827.3M, about $594M, to build a globally distributed AI inference cloud on Latitude. About A$369.5M goes to four AI infrastructure contracts with US technology companies. The rest funds 2,048 NVIDIA B300 GPUs for on-demand use from autumn 2026.
platform: Latitude.sh rents bare metal servers that deploy in as little as five seconds, plus Metal GPU clusters with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 and H100 GPUs. It also sells virtual machines, managed Kubernetes, block, file and object storage and managed PostgreSQL. Megaport's network connects its compute to public clouds and more than 1,000 data centers.
outlook: Latitude plans to turn its bare metal platform into an on-demand inference cloud built on B300 GPUs and Megaport's private network. Delivering the four US AI contracts is the main near-term use of the new capital. Gui Soubihe remains CEO under Megaport.

name: Massed Compute
snippet: US GPU cloud founded in 2021 that rents NVIDIA GPUs from A30 to B300 on demand from $0.43 an hour. It says it owns and runs all its own hardware in Tier III data centers.
origin: Massed Compute started in 2021 because its founders saw demand for GPU compute outrunning supply, with available capacity too expensive and opaque. Rather than resell capacity, it bought its own hardware, built its own network and wrote software that provisions instances in about 90 seconds.
today: Massed Compute rents NVIDIA GPUs from A30 and A40 up to H200, B200 and B300 by the hour, with a one-hour minimum and no contracts. It also sells single-tenant bare metal servers, InfiniBand GPU clusters of 8 to more than 512 nodes and on-premise GPU servers. It is an NVIDIA Preferred Partner with SOC 2 Type II certification and does not publish fleet size, revenue or data center locations.
platform: On-demand instances come with CUDA preinstalled, an included virtual desktop and no bandwidth charges, and the company offers ready templates for tools such as JupyterLab and Ollama. A REST API and MCP endpoint let teams provision from their own tooling. The company says engineers on its own staff manage every server, switch and cable, with no third-party rackspace.
outlook: Massed Compute competes on posted hourly prices for small teams and adds clusters and on-premise servers for larger buyers. Its website lists no outside funding and no data center locations.
